evidence: src/application/order-service.ts: constructor injects ProductRepository and OrderRepository ports, so there is no direct persistence code
placeOrder: rolls back reservations with release() if any reserve() fails, so the order is all-or-nothing (application coordination)
advance: gets the next status from domain nextState(); cancel uses domain assertCancellable() to check the transition
Borderline: placeOrder checks for an empty order and that each line.quantity is a positive integer, then builds the Order literal with status 'placed'. A domain factory could own this.

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
OrderService is a typical application service. It loads data through the injected ProductRepository and OrderRepository ports, uses domain functions for the core rules (reserve, release, dispatch, nextState, assertCancellable, isOrderStatus, toStockLevel), saves results through the ports and runs compensating rollback across several products. It does no persistence, transport or framework work itself; the only platform call is randomUUID for id generation.

There is one borderline area. placeOrder checks itself that an order has lines and that quantities are positive integers, merges duplicate lines, and builds the Order with status "placed". cancel and advance set order.status directly. A stricter reviewer could say order creation rules and status changes belong in a domain factory or method. Still, checking input at the use-case boundary and assembling the result fit the application role, and the real state-transition rules (nextState, assertCancellable) and stock rules stay in the domain. Nothing here clearly belongs to another layer kind, so the file passes with moderate confidence.
